notes:
Summary: GildedFort is a long-standing defense contractor that needs an air-gapped private inference solution for handling classified and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). They cannot use hosted APIs. Key asks: installable on isolated racks, FIPS/KMS integration, signed model artifacts, deterministic model pinning, and an offline model catalog with signed manifests.

Customer quotes / call snippets: "Cannot have egress under any circumstance — model updates must be manual and auditable." "We need documented STIG/SCAP alignment and an integration pattern for our HSMs."

Technical constraints:
- Strict network isolation (no NTP to internet unless via internal stratum).
- Requirement for HSM-backed key wrap (FIPS 140-2/3) for model encryption at rest and transport inside the enclave.
- Appliances will run on vendor-supplied racks (dual 600GBps RDMA fabrics) and mixed GPU pool: A2-like inference accelerators + some x86 inference hosts.
- Must support quantized model variants (4-bit/8-bit) and an offline compilation step so kernels are pre-warmed before POC runs.
- Directory of model artifacts will be imported via signed USB media or internal artifact-repo mirror; need verification flow.

POC success criteria (customer):
- baseline latency: tail p95 < 120ms for chat prompts ~512 tokens on representative model (quantized)
- throughput: sustained 80 reqs/s per rack for embeddings batch workload with acceptable CPU overhead
- security: pass internal pen-test and receive documented STIG artifact mapping
- operations: documented OS/hypervisor checklist, playbooks for offline model upgrades, and automated audit logs shipped to on-prem SIEM

Decision process / stakeholders: procurement + program manager (M. Ralston), CISO Review Board (final sign-off), platform ops lead (Lt. Commander J. Hale), prime integrator (Novara Systems) evaluating integration effort.

Artifacts linked: security Q + initial architecture slide deck, lab rack spec, and a brief TCO sketch. POC budget approved subject to STIG findings.
